title: A method to evaluate enhanced rock weathering using intact soil monoliths under field conditions
author: Zani, Barneze, et al.

steps.title: Record site location and climate data
steps.instruction: Note the experimental site coordinates (Cockle Park Farm, 55.2144° N, −1.6854° W) and the monolith source site (RAF Leeming, 54.2865° N, −1.5168° W). Record the climate for the monitoring period (average temperature 8.4 °C, total precipitation 749.8 mm, maximum 25 °C, minimum −4 °C). Document the soil type (Cambisol, loam) and its properties: organic C ≈2 %, inorganic C ≈0.2 %, pH 6.3, sand 36.5 %, silt 40.9 %, clay 22.2 %.

steps.title: Fabricate PVC components for monolith system
steps.instruction: Acquire standard PVC plumbing parts from a supplier (e.g., Plastics Express, UK). Cut 200 mm‑diameter PVC pipe (wall thickness 5 mm) into 450 mm segments. Drill two 20 mm holes in one end, spaced ~25 mm from that end, and bevel the opposite end to create a cutting edge. Obtain a PVC double‑socket coupling (200 mm diameter, 200 mm length, 5 mm wall). Glue a 5 mm‑thick acrylic ring base (Kitronik, UK) into the centre of the coupling, then insert a stainless‑steel mesh (grade 304, 5.1 mm aperture, Mesh Direct), a woven weed‑control mesh (70 GSM, Jardim Perfect Garden), and a geotextile membrane (Spudlica, 100 gsm, 100 µm mesh). Prepare a PVC end socket plug: drill a central 6 mm hole, insert a 6 mm bulkhead threaded‑to‑tube adaptor (RS, UK), and fix a 5 mm acrylic layer to the inner bottom for levelling. Obtain a polyurethane sampling tube (minimum 500 mm length, 6 mm diameter, RS, UK).

steps.title: Collect intact soil monolith using PVC pipe
steps.instruction: Place the sectioned PVC pipe on the chosen plot with the two 20 mm holes facing upward and the beveled end in contact with the soil surface. Lay a wooden block on top of the pipe and use a tractor‑mounted front loader to push the pipe into the ground until the soil surface is ~25 mm above the pipe’s upper end. Thread a 6 mm polypropylene rope through the two holes, attach it to the front loader, and pull upward to extract the intact soil core, keeping the soil undisturbed inside the pipe.

steps.title: Assemble monolith with double socket and plug
steps.instruction: Fit the prepared double‑socket coupling onto the beveled end of the pipe that now contains the intact soil monolith, ensuring the geotextile membrane contacts the bottom of the monolith and the acrylic ring base prevents sliding. Attach the socket plug (with the 6 mm adaptor) to the opposite end of the double socket, sealing the system. Connect the polyurethane sampling tube to the bulkhead adaptor, completing the fluid‑sampling assembly.

steps.title: Install assembled system in field trench
steps.instruction: Excavate a trench or cylindrical hole 400 mm deep and 200 mm wide using a tractor, post‑hole borer, or drill. Position the assembled monolith system within the trench and backfill soil around the PVC pipe. Ensure approximately 50 mm of the pipe protrudes above the ground surface and that the sampling‑tube outlet is accessible for leachate collection.

steps.title: Collect leachate samples over experimental period
steps.instruction: Allow water to percolate through the soil monolith and travel via the sampling tube to the collection point. Collect leachate continuously (or at regular intervals) for the intended monitoring duration (e.g., 6 months from November 2023 to April 2024, with the experiment continuing up to 9 months). Store samples appropriately for later chemical analysis.

steps.title: Analyze leachate chemistry and calculate fluxes
steps.instruction: Analyse each leachate sample for bicarbonate (HCO₃⁻), calcium (Ca²⁺), magnesium (Mg²⁺), and pH. Use the measured concentrations together with the known leachate volume to compute solute fluxes for each treatment (control, basalt 20 t ha⁻¹, biochar 5 t ha⁻¹, basalt + biochar 20 + 5 t ha⁻¹). Compare fluxes across treatments to assess enhanced rock weathering efficacy.
